research_question: Among adults undergoing cardiac surgery, what is the effect of perioperative levosimendan compared with placebo on all-cause mortality?
outcome_description: All-cause mortality, analyzed as the number of deaths among the total number randomized in each arm at the mortality time point reported by each eligible trial; each trial contributes one mortality comparison to the primary pool.
positive_direction: For directionally harmonized effects, a positive effect means levosimendan favors survival by reducing all-cause mortality compared with placebo; for the requested Risk Ratio itself, RR < 1 favors levosimendan and RR > 1 favors placebo.
search_queries: levosimendan placebo cardiac surgery randomized trial mortality
levosimendan cardiac surgical patients controlled trial deaths
perioperative levosimendan placebo cardiac surgery survival outcome
inclusion_criteria: Original empirical studies enrolling adults undergoing any cardiac surgical procedure and evaluating perioperative levosimendan against placebo.
Studies reporting all-cause deaths and randomized totals by treatment arm, or sufficient quantitative information to derive those values and a Risk Ratio.
Any eligible publication status, setting, language, cardiac procedure, levosimendan regimen, and reported mortality follow-up duration.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical study, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, commentaries, and theoretical papers.
No comparison between a levosimendan treatment condition and a placebo control condition.

No quantitative outcome data capable of producing an effect size, such as arm-specific deaths and totals, proportions, odds ratios, or other sufficient statistics; means with SDs or t/F values alone are insufficient for this binary mortality analysis unless deaths and denominators can also be recovered.
Completely unrelated to levosimendan use in adults undergoing cardiac surgery.
moderators_to_extract: Cardiac surgery type, including CABG, valve, combined, or other procedures
Baseline ventricular function or low-cardiac-output risk profile
Levosimendan dose, loading dose use, infusion duration, and timing relative to surgery
Mortality follow-up duration and mortality definition
Study design characteristics, including multicenter status and risk-of-bias domains
Participant age, sex distribution, and randomized sample size
effect_size_note: Pool arm-level all-cause mortality as Risk Ratios using each trial's reported number of deaths and total randomized per arm, preferably according to the randomized assignment/available intention-to-treat denominator. Use a random-effects primary model with a 95% confidence interval and report a fixed-effect sensitivity analysis if appropriate. Trials with zero deaths in both arms are not estimable for an RR and must be excluded from the pooled estimate without adding a continuity correction; list them separately and report their randomized sample sizes. For trials with zero deaths in only one arm, use the prespecified software's standard single-zero handling and assess sensitivity to alternative continuity-correction methods. Avoid double-counting overlapping reports, selecting the most complete mortality dataset for each trial. Assess heterogeneity with tau-squared, I-squared, and Cochran's Q; evaluate influence/leave-one-out results and risk-of-bias sensitivity analyses. Assess small-study effects with funnel plots and an appropriate regression test only if enough estimable studies are available. Follow PRISMA 2020 for searching, duplicate removal, dual screening, extraction, risk-of-bias assessment, study flow, excluded-study reasons, synthesis reporting, and certainty assessment.
